scenes.title: The concept — set-builder language
scenes.visualNotes: math-board sequential reveal — One concept → Set-builder → Membership → Representative.

beats.label: One concept
beats.detail: Membership in [x] — the equivalence class of x

beats.label: Representative
beats.detail: x is the chosen label for the bucket

beats.say:
Hi friends, welcome back. This is Turner.
One concept today: membership in an equivalence class.
beats.visualNotes:
math-board heading: Equivalence class membership
reveal: One concept — Membership in [x], the equivalence class of x.

beats.say:
Pick a representative x. The class is every y tied to x by the relation.
Textbook set-builder: all y such that x is related to y.
beats.visualNotes:
math-board: [x] = { y ∈ X | x ~ y }
emphasis: [x], ∈, ~

beats.say:
Formal membership: y is in the class of x if and only if x is related to y.
That biconditional is the whole idea — nothing else in this clip.
beats.visualNotes:
math-board: y ∈ [x]  ↔  x ~ y
emphasis: ↔, ∈
then Representative — x is the chosen label for the bucket.

scenes.title: Turn-Lang vs Lean — same biconditional
scenes.visualNotes: Side-by-side compare — caption beats on both sides at each say line.

beats.say: Same concept in Turn-Lang and Lean — who reads closer to the textbook?
beats.visualNotes: Open both panes. Point at the named Turn structure versus Lean theorem title.

lean.code:
theorem eqvClass_mem_iff (x y : α) :
  y ∈ s.eqvClass x ↔ s x y := by
  simp [Setoid.eqvClass]

beats.say: Turn names the bucket: EquivalenceClass, with representative x and relation E.
beats.visualNotes: Highlight representative x and relation E on Turn; Setoid packaging on Lean.

beats.say: The def law is exactly set-builder membership: y in the class if and only if x is related to y.
beats.visualNotes: Caption both sides on the biconditional / def law.

beats.say: Lean packages the relation in a Setoid — the class is eqvClass x, a computed set.
beats.visualNotes: Contrast Turn membership law with Lean computed eqvClass.

beats.say: Membership is still a biconditional — but the bucket is not its own structure with an explicit law block.
beats.visualNotes: Keep both panes; stress Turn's named law block versus Lean infrastructure.

beats.say: Lean proves it by unfolding eqvClass; Turn states the law where the book puts the definition.
beats.visualNotes: Lean simp unfold vs Turn def law in source.

beats.say: For teaching the meaning of equivalence class, Turn's named structure matches the book line for line.
beats.visualNotes: Hold both panes for the teaching claim; next scene is the math-board verdict.

scenes.title: Verdict — who is closer to the original meaning?
scenes.visualNotes: math-board verdict — Textbook → Turn-Lang → Lean 4 → Verdict callout.

beats.label: Textbook
beats.detail: [x] = { y | x ~ y }  and  y ∈ [x] ↔ x ~ y

beats.label: Turn-Lang
beats.detail: EquivalenceClass + def law: y ∈ self ↔ (x,y) ∈ E

beats.label: Lean 4
beats.detail: y ∈ s.eqvClass x ↔ s x y  (unfold eqvClass to see the set)

beats.label: Verdict
beats.detail: Turn names the bucket where the book does

beats.say: Textbook: a set of y values, membership spelled as a biconditional with the relation.
beats.visualNotes:
math-board heading: Who matches the textbook?
Textbook: [x] = { y | x ~ y } and y ∈ [x] ↔ x ~ y

beats.say: Turn: EquivalenceClass is that set, def law is the biconditional — visible in source and render.
beats.visualNotes: math-board: Turn-Lang — EquivalenceClass + def law: y ∈ self ↔ (x,y) ∈ E

beats.say: Lean: correct math, but eqvClass is infrastructure — you unfold to see the set-builder meaning.
beats.visualNotes: math-board: Lean 4 — y ∈ s.eqvClass x ↔ s x y (unfold eqvClass to see the set)

beats.say: Verdict: Turn-Lang stays closer to how the concept is introduced on the page.
